response.answer: No, the compliance deadline did not change. Document 2025-03118 (90 FR 10592, published 2025-02-25) delayed the effective date of the 'healthy' claim final rule (2024-29957, 89 FR 106064) from February 25, 2025 to April 28, 2025, in accordance with the Presidential memorandum 'Regulatory Freeze Pending Review.' However, the document explicitly states: 'We note that the compliance date remains unchanged at this time.' The compliance date of February 25, 2028, as originally stated in 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064), remains in effect. This is confirmed by the timeline facts, which show the compliance date of 2028-02-25 with no supersession entries. A delay of an effective date does not move a compliance date unless a document says so, and here the delaying document (2025-03118) affirmatively confirms the compliance date is unchanged.

answer_rows.product: Any food bearing a 'healthy' nutrient content claim
answer_rows.required_change: Ensure food meets the new food-group-equivalent and nutrients-to-limit criteria in 21 CFR 101.65(d) if bearing a 'healthy' (or derivative) implied nutrient content claim

response.answer:
Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify for one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient foods from encouraged food groups, or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to bear the 'healthy' claim:

1. **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement**: The food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups encouraged by the Dietary Guidelines (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free or low-fat dairy, lean meat/seafood/eggs/beans/peas/lentils/nuts/seeds). The specific FGE amounts vary by product category (individual food, mixed product, main dish, or meal) as set forth in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v) and the associated tables. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3); 89 FR 106064)

2. **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement**: The food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, expressed as a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients. These limits also vary by product category. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v); 89 FR 106064; see also 90 FR 10592 at passage describing the rule as requiring 'FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients')

As summarized in the background section of 90 FR 10592 (Doc. 2025-03118): the rule 'requires that, to bear a claim subject to the rule, individual food products, mixed products, main dishes, and meals must meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients.'

answer_rows.required_change: Food must (1) contain a qualifying food group equivalent (FGE) amount and (2) meet nutrient-to-limit (NTL) caps for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, unless it qualifies for an automatic exemption under § 101.65(d)(3)(i) or (vi).

response.answer: The 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim is governed by 21 CFR 101.65(d). This section defines the general nutritional claims paragraph that covers labeling claims which are implied nutrient content claims because they suggest that a food may help consumers maintain healthy dietary practices due to its nutrient content. The general framework for implied nutrient content claims (including 'healthy') is also set out in 21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii), which defines an implied nutrient content claim as one that 'suggests that a food, because of its nutrient content, may be useful in maintaining healthy dietary practices, where there is also implied or explicit information about the nutrition content of the food (e.g., "healthy")' (passage cfr-21-101.13@2025-04-28#0000). The final rule updating the definition of 'healthy' was published at 89 FR 106064 (Doc. 2024-29957, published 2024-12-27), with an effective date of April 28, 2025 (as revised by Doc. 2025-03118), and a compliance date of February 25, 2028 (stated by 2024-29957). The amendatory instructions in that final rule specifically direct revision of § 101.65 paragraphs (a)(2) and (d) (passage 2024-29957#0002).

answer_rows.trigger: Final rule 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064) revising the definition of 'healthy' under 21 CFR 101.65(d)
answer_rows.required_change: Products using the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must meet the updated criteria in 21 CFR 101.65(d) as revised (food group equivalent requirements, nutrient limits per RACC, etc.)

response.answer:
The Red No. 3 order (90 FR 4628, Doc. 2025-00830, published 2025-01-16) changes two CFR provisions in 21 CFR Part 74, but they do NOT all change on the same day:

1. **21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use): Amendatory instruction 2 removes this section, and amendatory instruction 3 revises § 74.1303 to incorporate the identity and specifications previously cross-referenced from § 74.303. Both of these take effect on **January 15, 2027** (2025-00830#0000; timeline-facts).

2. **21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs): Amendatory instruction 4 removes this section, effective **January 18, 2028** (2025-00830#0002; timeline-facts).

Specifically, the amendatory instructions are:
- Instruction 2: Remove § 74.303 — effective January 15, 2027.
- Instruction 3: Revise § 74.1303 (to add identity/specifications from § 74.303 so the ingested-drug listing is self-contained after § 74.303 is removed) — effective January 15, 2027.
- Instruction 4: Remove § 74.1303 — effective January 18, 2028.

These effective dates were confirmed by 91 FR 50475 (Doc. 2026-15920, published 2026-08-05), which lifted the administrative stay that had been in place from February 18, 2025, through August 5, 2026 (2026-15920#0000). The stay did not move any dates.

The order sets no separate compliance date. Because this is a revocation (not a new requirement with a phase-in), the operative deadline for each provision is derived from its effective date: after that date, use of FD&C Red No. 3 renders the food or drug adulterated (2025-00830#0021).

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This carve-out means that a food bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d) does not need to include the § 101.13(h) disclosure statement, even if the food would otherwise trigger it. All other provisions of § 101.13 (e.g., type size requirements in (f), general claim requirements in (b), substitute food provisions in (d), etc.) still apply to a 'healthy' claim.

answer_rows.trigger: Use of the term 'healthy' or its derivatives as an implied nutrient content claim under 21 CFR 101.65(d)
answer_rows.required_change: Must comply with all general requirements of 21 CFR 101.13 except § 101.13(h) (the nutrient disclosure statement requirement is carved out for 'healthy' claims made under § 101.65(d))
